f_h_hz.name: f_h_hz
f_h_hz.method: saturated VMAC issue rate; CHAINS sweep 1/2/4/8, ITERS slope fit on npu_time
evidence: plateau: 1.015/1.019/1.013 G VMAC/s at chains=2/4/8 (within 0.6%) -> pipe saturated, latency hidden
chains=1 (1.92 ns/iter) == chains=2 (1.97 ns/iter): 1 chain is latency-bound, 2 fill the pipe
chains=4 -> 8 throughput ratio 0.994x: plateau, not still-scaling
disassembly (llvm-objdump, aie2): loop .LBB0_1 unrolled 4x (r5=0x3e8=ITERS, add r5,r5,#-0x4); 16 bundles / 16 vmac in body incl. branch delay slots => exactly 1 VMAC per bundle
bundle count x measured slope: 4 cycles/iter / 3.9244 ns = 1.019 GHz, agrees with the plateau independently
caveats: assumes 1 bundle/cycle issue (standard VLIW model); the plateau corroborates but does not prove it
measured at pmode=default; setting pmode needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN. Do not assume clock-invariance across modes.
npu_time basis; cold-vs-warm does not affect the slope (fixed cost cancels)

c_cmd_s.name: c_cmd_s
c_cmd_s.method: near-null kernel (touch each input once, write one word), warmed, median device npu_time
evidence: across both runs the floor sits in 148.7-162.0 us; point estimate 155 us (+/-5%)
independent corroboration: K1 chains=1 fit intercept ~236 us on a larger graph, same order
caveats: THIS IS THE DOMINANT TERM ON npu1: a do-nothing dispatch costs ~155 us of device time. For scale, R64 measured aie2p full production QKV device span at 241 us.
warmed medians; cold first-command values are far higher (R63 saw 3.5-4.2 ms cold vs 1.03 ms warm)
measured at n_bos 2-3 only; see c_bo_s

c_bo_s.name: c_bo_s
c_bo_s.method: BO-count sweep slope; not separable from noise
evidence: run A slope = -5.130 us/BO (negative => unphysical => noise-dominated)
run B slope = +4.600 us/BO; the sign flips between runs
conclusion: |c_bo| < ~5 us, indistinguishable from zero, and <3% of the 155 us floor
caveats: value 0.0 is a bounded measurement (|c_bo| < 5 us), not an extrapolation

sweep is BLOCKED above n_bos=3: nargs>=3 fails aiecc with "Resource allocation pipeline failed" at tile(0,2) — a core tile cannot source that many input DMA channels. The 5-slot H4 limit is never reached because the per-core DMA channel limit binds first.

bw_feed_bytes_s.name: bw_feed_bytes_s
bw_feed_bytes_s.method: tile stream, 1 word touched per tile; slope of npu_time vs bytes at 4 columns
evidence: cols=1: 4.097 GB/s (fixed 228.2 us)
cols=2: 7.637 GB/s (fixed 176.7 us)
cols=4: 16.147 GB/s (fixed 181.9 us)
caveats: slope basis: the C1 dispatch floor lands in the intercept, not the bandwidth
cheapest possible consumer; a real kernel may not reach this feed rate
halo's 14.4/56.5 GB/s are aie2p on Strix Halo and do not transfer

bw_drain_bytes_s.name: bw_drain_bytes_s
bw_drain_bytes_s.method: core writes 1 word/tile, DMA drains; slope of npu_time vs bytes at 4 columns
evidence: cols=1: 4.140 GB/s (fixed 210.5 us)
cols=2: 8.149 GB/s (fixed 183.4 us)
cols=4: 15.916 GB/s (fixed 172.2 us)
caveats: slope basis; C1 floor lands in the intercept
measured separately from feed because R64 found drain, not feed, was the limiter

c_task_issue_s.name: c_task_issue_s
c_task_issue_s.method: 8 MiB payload held constant; tile-size sweep varies task count 8x (4096 -> 512). Slope of npu_time vs task count.
evidence: fitted slope moved 9.8 ns -> 3.3 ns/task between runs; point estimate 5 ns with the sign stable but the magnitude not
even at 4096 tasks this is ~20 us against a ~2280 us transfer: under 1%
caveats: FINDING — THE aie2p PRIOR DOES NOT TRANSFER. R68 cut tasks ~3x on halo for 24% less time; on npu1 an 8x cut buys ~1.5%. Reason: npu1 feeds at ~3.7 GB/s/column, so a 2 KiB tile takes ~553 ns to move while task issue costs ~5 ns — the overhead hides completely behind the transfer. halo moves bytes ~3.5x faster per column, which is what made per-task cost visible there. Task-count optimisation is NOT a lever on npu1.
value is an upper bound, not a fit: below the noise floor at these sizes
single column; concurrent multi-column issue is unmeasured
tile=32 KiB failed to build: 32 KiB x depth-2 double buffer = 64 KiB = exactly L1 (M1). M1 binds the tile size.

fill_drain_s.name: fill_drain_s
fill_drain_s.method: fifo-depth sweep at constant payload; per-depth residual over the best pipelined time
evidence: depth=1: 1252.06 us
depth=2: 1231.90 us
depth=3: 1228.28 us
depth=4: 1225.03 us
depth=8: 1229.91 us
depth1 -> best(4): 1.022x
caveats: small term on npu1: the C1 dispatch floor (~155 us) dwarfs it
L1 (M1) bounds depth*tile_bytes; aie2p saw depth-4 build failures for the same reason (R58/E2)

bw_feed_per_col_bytes_s.name: bw_feed_per_col_bytes_s
bw_feed_per_col_bytes_s.method: per-column feed rate; C2 column sweep is near-linear so bandwidth is modelled as per_col * columns
evidence: cols=1: 4.097 GB/s
linear within ~4%: 4.03 GB/s/col x 4 = 16.1 GB/s, matches the measured 4-col roof
caveats: broadcast pattern (every column reads the same stream); R56 found shared vs distinct made no difference on aie2p, unverified here
cheapest possible consumer — a real kernel may not reach this rate

bw_drain_per_col_bytes_s.name: bw_drain_per_col_bytes_s
bw_drain_per_col_bytes_s.method: per-column drain rate from the C5 column sweep
evidence: cols=1: 4.140 GB/s
feed and drain are SYMMETRIC on npu1 (16.147 vs 15.916 GB/s at 4 cols) — unlike halo, where R64 found the output DMA starved 198 us of a 241 us span
caveats: near-linear in columns, same as feed

cyc_per_vmac.method: ISA: 1 vmac per bundle in the unrolled chain loop; hardware: VMAC/s == f_H at saturation
evidence: (4, 8, 8): vmac/call=1.00, MACs/vmac=256
(8, 8, 8): vmac/call=2.00, MACs/vmac=256
(4, 16, 8): vmac/call=2.00, MACs/vmac=256
(2, 8, 8): vmac/call=1.00, MACs/vmac=128
(4, 8, 8): 268.17 G MACs/s/core (264 MACs/cycle)
(8, 8, 8): 258.05 G MACs/s/core (254 MACs/cycle)
(4, 16, 8): 260.59 G MACs/s/core (257 MACs/cycle)
(2, 8, 8): 129.85 G MACs/s/core (128 MACs/cycle)

macs_per_native_vmac_int8_int4.name: macs_per_native_vmac_int8_int4
macs_per_native_vmac_int8_int4.method: int8 x int4 (mmul_8_4): MACs per source mac() / native vmacs; confirmed by measured MACs/s
evidence: ISA <4,16,8,int8,int4>: 1 vmac/call, 512 MACs => 512 MACs/VMAC (NATIVE)
HW <4,16,8,int8,int4>: 520.09 G MACs/s = 512.4 MACs/cycle — exactly 2x int8 x int8
HW <8,16,8>: 522.82 G MACs/s; HW <4,32,8>: 524.98 G MACs/s (both VIRTUAL, same rate)
VMAC/s is ~1.01-1.03 G across every shape AND dtype: the issue rate is fixed at f_H, only MACs-per-VMAC changes
caveats: THIS IS WHERE >16 TOPS COMES FROM: 16 x 512 x 2 x 1.015 GHz = 16.63 TOPS, matching the ~16 TOPS marketing figure. The claim is int8 x int4, NOT dense int8 x int8.
directly relevant to hipfire: OQ4/MQ4 are 4-bit weight formats, so the quant path gets 2x
mmul_8_4 has its OWN shape family (4x16x8, 8x16x8, 4x32x8); int8 shapes are invalid for it
optimal shape is <4,16,8,int8,int4> — native and fills the VMAC

f_h_pmode_invariant.name: f_h_pmode_invariant
f_h_pmode_invariant.method: re-ran K1 chains=4 under pmode=turbo via passwordless sudo, compared against default
evidence: default: 1019.3 MHz (0.981 ns/VMAC)
turbo: 988.5 MHz (1.011 ns/VMAC)
turbo is a NO-OP for the AIE compute clock — 3% slower, within run-to-run noise
matches halo/aie2p findings: turbo 15.21 vs 15.7 TOPS, compute clock already maxed under load
caveats: pmode restored to default after the test
rules OUT clock as the explanation for >16 TOPS; the answer is int4 (see macs_per_native_vmac_int8_int4)

macs_per_native_vmac_int8_int8.name: macs_per_native_vmac_int8_int8
macs_per_native_vmac_int8_int8.method: int8 x int8: MACs per source mac() / native vmacs emitted; confirmed by measured MACs/s
evidence: ISA <4,8,8>: 1 vmac/call, 256 MACs => 256 MACs/VMAC (NATIVE)
ISA <8,8,8>: 2 vmac/call, 512 MACs => 256 MACs/VMAC (VIRTUAL)
HW <4,8,8>: 258.68 G MACs/s = 254.9 MACs/cycle
HW <8,8,8>: 258.84 G MACs/s = 255.0 MACs/cycle — 2x the time per call, IDENTICAL throughput
HW <2,8,8>: 130.47 G MACs/s = 128.5 MACs/cycle (half-fills the VMAC)
caveats: mmul<8,8,8> is VIRTUAL on AIE2 (native on AIE2P) — it buys nothing here
optimal int8 x int8 shape is <4,8,8>
dense int8 peak = 16 x 256 x 2 x 1.015 GHz = 8.31 TOPS — HALF the ~16 TOPS figure
